hero.title: Post-procedure protocol built on metabolic graft protection, photobiomodulation, HBOT and LADD.
hero.lead: The first 48 hours determine graft survival. Instead of saline and passive healing — an integrated plan combining transplantology-grade preservation solutions, 650/830 nm photobiomodulation, hyperbaric oxygen therapy at 1.5–3.0 ATA and laser-assisted drug delivery (LADD).
hero.subLead: 48 hours = the critical window for graft survival. Full recovery is guided systematically across the first 14 days.
hero.stat1v: PBM wavelengths applied immediately after the procedure
hero.stat2v: HBOT session pressure on day 0 and day 1
hero.stat3v: target temperature for HypoThermosol + ATP-v solution
hero.stat4v: critical graft ischaemia window before revascularisation

dayTips.headline: Procedure day
dayTips.tip: First PBM (650/830 nm) and HBOT (1.5–3.0 ATA) session on the same day. Sleep semi-upright ≥30°. Do not touch the scalp.

dayTips.headline: Critical reperfusion window
dayTips.tip: Second HBOT session. 20-min PBM. Touch-free saline/HOCl spray every 2–3 h. No hats.

dayTips.headline: Graft stabilisation
dayTips.tip: HOCl rinsing from 48 h, touch-free stream. 20–30 min walk without bending forward. PBM 20 min.

dayTips.headline: Swelling peak
dayTips.tip: Forehead and eyelid swelling peaks on day 2–3. Sleep ≥30°, cool compresses on the forehead (never on the grafts).

dayTips.headline: First wash
dayTips.tip: Emollient → lukewarm water from the palms → mild pH 5.5 shampoo → microfibre towel (no rubbing). No SLS.

dayTips.headline: Microbiome management
dayTips.tip: Wash 1×/day. Light activity OK without sweating on the scalp. Continue PBM daily.

dayTips.headline: Erythema check
dayTips.tip: Trichoscopy follow-up photo. If redness stays intense — contact your coordinator.

dayTips.headline: Week 1 — report
dayTips.tip: Checkpoint: weekly report (anagen %, tolerance). Video call with the coordinator.

dayTips.headline: Crusts come off
dayTips.tip: From day 8 soft fingertip massage during washing. Crusts shed on their own — do not scratch or peel.

dayTips.headline: Microbiome + hydration
dayTips.tip: HOCl mist 2–3×/day. Anti-inflammatory diet: omega-3, polyphenols, protein 1.2–1.6 g/kg.

dayTips.headline: Donor area
dayTips.tip: PBM with special focus on the donor area. Optional cold atmospheric plasma (CAP).

dayTips.headline: Back to everyday life
dayTips.tip: Return to moderate sport (no overhead barbells). Loose hat is OK in the sun — never tight.

dayTips.headline: Consolidation
dayTips.tip: Wash with standard pH 5.5 shampoo. Gentle conditioner OK. No hair dye for at least 4 weeks.

dayTips.headline: Preparing for follow-up
dayTips.tip: Schedule the 14-day check-up. Full photo set in the same angles as before the procedure.

dayTips.headline: End of the critical protocol
dayTips.tip: Crusts gone. Continue PBM, minoxidil, HBOT per the long-term plan. UPF 50+ sun protection. Shock loss (week 2–6) is expected.

pbm-650-vs-830.q: What is the difference between 650 nm and 830 nm in scalp photobiomodulation?
pbm-650-vs-830.a: 650 nm (red) penetrates 1–2 mm and acts mainly on the epidermis, dermis and hair papilla. 830 nm (near-infrared) reaches 3–5 mm — deeper follicles and oedematous subcutaneous tissue. Both activate cytochrome-c oxidase (complex IV of the respiratory chain), boosting mitochondrial ATP production.

first-wash.q: When can I wash my head after DHI?
first-wash.a: Gentle, touch-free rinsing of the recipient area with saline or HOCl — from 48 h. Full wash with a pH 5.5 SLS-free shampoo — from day 4. Rubbing and crust removal only after day 8. Early rubbing is the most common mechanical cause of graft loss.

hbot-nfz.q: Is HBOT after a hair transplant reimbursed by public healthcare?
hbot-nfz.a: No. Reimbursed indications include CO poisoning, decompression sickness, radionecrosis and diabetic foot. HBOT in hair transplantology is a commercial procedure performed in private centres.

minoxidil-oral.a: At 0.25–2.5 mg/day the safety profile in healthy adults is well documented (Sinclair 2018, Randolph & Tosti 2021). Requires medical qualification, blood pressure assessment and exclusion of cardiac contraindications. Not registered for this indication — used off-label.

prp-in-holding.q: Why use PRP in the graft holding solution?
prp-in-holding.a: Platelet-rich plasma contains VEGF, PDGF, EGF, IGF-1 and TGF-β. Incubating grafts in PRP before implantation saturates them with growth factors, accelerating angiogenesis and shortening the 48–72 h post-implant ischaemia window.

hypothermosol.q: How does HypoThermosol differ from saline?
hypothermosol.a: 0.9% NaCl has osmolarity ~308 mOsm/L and contains no energy buffer — cells stored in it at 4 °C exhaust ATP within 2–4 h. HypoThermosol FRS is a buffered hypothermic solution (HEPES, mannitol, adenosine, glutathione) designed for transplant organs, maintaining ionic homeostasis at 2–8 °C for over 24 h.

tulium-vs-plasma.q: Thulium 1927 nm laser or cold plasma — what to choose for LADD?
tulium-vs-plasma.a: Fractional thulium 1927 nm is the LADD standard: controlled microchannels 150–300 µm deep, short downtime, well-documented penetration of minoxidil and peptides. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) is non-thermal — it generates RONS and increases stratum corneum permeability without ablation, but drug delivery depth is smaller (~50–100 µm). Thulium: deeper penetration, more energy in tissue. CAP: safer directly over fresh grafts.

alcohol-nicotine.q: Can I drink alcohol and smoke after the procedure?
alcohol-nicotine.a: Nicotine causes peripheral vasoconstriction for up to 90 min after each dose — during the revascularisation window (day 0–7) it increases the risk of graft necrosis. Alcohol impairs haemostasis and increases swelling. Recommended abstinence: at least 14 days.

final-result.q: When will I see the final result?
final-result.a: Shock loss of transplanted hairs: weeks 2–6. Anagen entry: months 3–4. First visible density: month 6. Final result: 12–15 months after the procedure.

sport-sauna-sun.q: When can I return to sport, sauna, swimming pool and sun after DHI?
sport-sauna-sun.a: Light sport (walking, yoga without inversions) — from day 3. Strength training and running — from week 2, when crusts have shed. Dry and steam sauna — no earlier than 14 days post-procedure. Chlorinated pool — 14 days, sea water — 21 days. Direct sun — avoid for 30 days; then UPF 50+ hat. Tanning beds — 4 weeks.

first-48h-normal.q: What is normal in the first 48 hours after DHI?
first-48h-normal.a: On day 0–3 it is normal to have: mild forehead and temple swelling, slight redness in the recipient zone, a tight ‘squeezing’ sensation, tiny serum droplets on the grafts and mild pain responding to medication. These are signs of inflammation, micro-bleeding and fluid retention. Sleep semi-upright (≥30°) for the first 5 days.

forehead-swelling.q: Is forehead and face swelling after the procedure normal?
forehead-swelling.a: Yes — forehead, eyelid and upper-face swelling occurs in 60–80% of patients on days 1–3. It is due to post-procedure fluid migrating along the loose subcutaneous tissue of the forehead. Usually resolves in 48–72 h. Accelerated by: head-up sleep, cold compresses around (not on) the recipient area and prescribed medication.

pain-pressure.q: Is pain and pressure in the recipient area normal on day 0–3?
pain-pressure.a: Yes. A ‘tight’ feeling, mild pulsing or burning is typical for the acute inflammation phase. Pain should be easily controlled (paracetamol + ibuprofen). If pain worsens after day 2–3, with fever >38 °C, purulent discharge or spreading redness — contact the clinic.

scab-removal.q: When will crusts wash off and can I remove them myself?
scab-removal.a: Crusts form from day 2 and shed between day 7 and 14. Do not scratch them off or soak them under a strong stream — mechanical detachment can tear out a graft. From day 8 you may use a gentle fingertip massage during washing with a pH 5.5 shampoo.

itching.q: Is scalp itching during weeks 1–2 normal?
itching.a: Yes. Itching in the recipient area between day 4 and 10 is a sign of healing. Do not scratch. What helps: HOCl mist, mild shampoo, short antihistamine course after consultation. If itching is intense or accompanied by a rash — notify your coordinator.

shock-loss.q: Is shedding of transplanted hairs in weeks 2–6 normal?
shock-loss.a: Yes — this is shock loss. Transplanted hairs enter telogen and shed 2–6 weeks after the procedure. The bulbs remain in the skin. New hair starts to grow in months 3–4. PBM reduces shock loss severity.

call-clinic.q: When should I contact the clinic immediately?
call-clinic.a: Fever >38 °C after day 2, purulent discharge from the recipient area, rapidly spreading redness and warmth, severe pain not controlled by medication, bleeding >30 min, large bruises outside the forehead area, allergic reaction, visible graft loss.

sleep-position.q: Can I sleep on my side after a hair transplant?
sleep-position.a: For the first 4–5 days — sleep on your back with the head elevated ≥30° (wedge pillow). Side sleeping increases pressure and friction. From day 5 you may carefully try a side position. Full return after 10–14 days, once graft adhesion is stable.

day-0.q: Day 0 (procedure day) — what to do after coming home?
day-0.a: Do not remove the forehead band before the time noted on your card (usually 24 h). Sleep semi-upright (≥30°). Do not touch the recipient area. Do not wash the head. Avoid aspirin and NSAIDs unless prescribed — paracetamol is safe. Drink 2–3 L of water. The first PBM/HBOT session is usually on day 0 or +1.

day-1.a: Recipient area: small crusts, mild redness, tingling discomfort. Donor area: dull pain, tightness. Possible first signs of forehead swelling. Continue head-up sleep, cold compresses on the forehead, medication per your card. Allowed: a short walk, a light protein-rich meal.

day-2-hocl.q: Day 2 — when to start saline / HOCl spraying?
day-2-hocl.a: From 48 h start gentle, touch-free hydration of the recipient area with sterile saline or HOCl — spray from 15–20 cm every 2–3 h. Goal: a moist environment (faster revascularisation), softening crusts, limiting bacterial colonisation. Do not rub.

day-3-swelling-peak.q: Day 3 — peak of swelling, is it a reason to worry?
day-3-swelling-peak.a: No. Forehead, eyelid and nasal-bridge swelling peaks on day 2–3 and subsides in 48–72 h. What helps: sleep ≥30°, cold compresses, walking. Warning signs: asymmetric swelling with severe pain, neck/throat swelling, shortness of breath, rash — contact the clinic.

day-4-first-wash.q: Day 4 — the first wash: step by step?
day-4-first-wash.a: 1) Apply a thin layer of emollient to the recipient area; leave 15–20 min. 2) Rinse with lukewarm water from your palms — not from the shower head. 3) Foam a mild pH 5.5 (SLS-free) shampoo in your hands and dab the foam with fingertips, no rubbing. 4) Rinse with water from your palms. 5) Pat dry with a microfibre towel — no rubbing. Repeat 1×/day through day 14.

day-5-7-revasc.q: Day 5–7 — what happens to grafts biologically?
day-5-7-revasc.a: Revascularisation window: new capillaries grow from the recipient bed into the transplanted follicles. Grafts move from imbibition to inosculation. Supported by: oxygenation (HBOT, no nicotine), PBM 650/830 nm, avoiding blood pressure spikes and mechanical injury. Graft adhesion is weak — no tight hats.

day-8-10-massage.q: Day 8–10 — when can I gently massage the scalp?
day-8-10-massage.a: From day 8 — soft circular fingertip massage during washing. Helps crusts shed and improves microcirculation. Do not use nails, brushes or irrigators. Continue PBM per protocol. Return to office work is OK — redness decreases.

day-11-14.q: Day 11–14 — end of the critical phase, what next?
day-11-14.a: Most crusts shed by day 14. Recipient area: pink, smooth. Grafts stably anchored. You may: strength training, normal washing, a gentle conditioner. Still avoid sauna, swimming pool and intense sun until day 21–30. Book the 14-day follow-up and bring control photos.

post-erythema.q: Is recipient-area redness persisting for 2–4 weeks normal?
post-erythema.a: Yes. Pink-red discoloration persists in most patients for 2–6 weeks, and up to 8 weeks in fair skin. Soothed by: PBM 650 nm, UPF 50+, avoiding alcohol and sauna. Warning signs: warm, painful, spreading redness — consult (suspected folliculitis/cellulitis).

diet.q: What to eat and drink during days 0–14 to support healing?
diet.a: Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight/day. Vitamin C 500–1000 mg + zinc 15–25 mg — collagen cofactor. Iron, D3, B12 — if deficient. Omega-3 (2–3 g EPA/DHA). Water: 30–35 ml/kg. Avoid: alcohol (14 days), excess sugars, high-dose garlic/ginkgo/turmeric (antiplatelet effect).

journey.title: An educated patient is a cooperating patient.
journey.p1: A patient leaving the clinic with a bloodied head, without a plan and without contact — that is not just a bad experience. Post-procedure stress cortisol impairs cutaneous circulation. Anxiety meaningfully reduces scalp perfusion and increases the risk of mechanical graft loss (scratching, improper washing, early crust removal).
journey.p2: Every patient who logs into our site has access to online materials (full documentation and the latest regenerative / anti-aging medicine trends) as well as the “Patient Journey” e-book with instructions for each of the first 14 days — what to do in the morning, in the evening, what not to do, when to worry. Plus: direct contact with the supervising doctor for the first 30 days.

Red flags requiring clinic contact

why.title: The window that decides the fate of every transplanted hair.
paragraphs: After DHI extraction the graft is an ischemic tissue. From the moment it is harvested until revascularization in the recipient bed, it survives only through oxygen diffusion from the plasma surrounding the implantation site. The first capillaries usually reach the dermal papilla between 48–96 h. For the hypoxic follicle this is a critical window that determines the final outcome of the procedure.

During this time the bulge stem cells and dermal papilla cells (DPC) consume their ATP reserves. Once depleted, apoptosis is triggered. Every hour of hypoxia is a measurable loss in the pool of viable follicles.
Post-operative cortisol is a vasoconstrictor. Anxiety, pain and misinformation genuinely impair scalp perfusion — which is why coordinated aftercare is not an add-on but a clinical parameter.

exVivo.title: Metabolic protection of grafts from the moment of extraction.
exVivo.lead: Many clinics still default to 0.9% saline or Ringer's solution. From a transplantation standpoint these maintain osmolarity but do not protect cellular metabolism. In our protocol grafts are transferred to solutions used in solid-organ preservation.

card1.title: HypoThermosol FRS + liposomal ATP (ATP-v)
card1.body: HypoThermosol FRS is a buffered hypothermic solution containing HEPES, mannitol, adenosine, glutathione and dextran. It maintains cellular ionic homeostasis at 2–8 °C for over 24 h. Adding liposomal ATP delivers energy directly into the cytosol — Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps keep working, osmotic pressure does not collapse, apoptosis is silenced.
card1.mech: 0.9% saline: ATP depleted in 2–4 h. HypoThermosol + ATP-v: > 90% cell viability after 12 h ex vivo.

card2.title: Graft bath in PRP before implantation
card2.body: Autologous platelet-rich plasma (1.5–6× baseline platelet concentration) incubates the grafts for 10–20 min before implantation. Growth factors (VEGF, PDGF-BB, EGF, IGF-1, TGF-β) saturate the follicle before placement, shortening the ischemic window and accelerating angiogenesis.
card2.mech: VEGF → endothelial proliferation; PDGF → pericyte migration; IGF-1 → maintenance of anagen in bulge stem cells.

pbm.title: 650 and 830 nm light as a bioenergetic tool.

card1.title: Post-procedure session parameters
bullets: 650 nm (red) — 1–2 mm penetration, epidermis and dermal papilla
830 nm (NIR) — 3–5 mm penetration, deep papillae, recipient bed
Dose 4–6 J/cm² per session (biostimulation threshold per Arndt-Schulz curve)
Irradiation of recipient and donor area immediately after the procedure
Sessions continued every 24–48 h for 14 days

card2.title: In-office equipment
card2.body: We use three LED lamps with verified emission spectra (red 630–660 nm and NIR 810–840 nm). Spectral measurement confirms compliance with the therapeutic range described in the literature (e.g. Avci et al. 2014, Hamblin 2016). The in-office session is continued at home by the patient with an LLLT helmet 2× daily/week for 12 weeks.
card2.mech: PBM also activates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in dermal papilla cells — key for entering the anagen phase.

hbot.title: Oxygen reaches where red blood cells cannot yet go.
hbot.lead: At 1.5–3.0 ATA breathing 100% O₂, arterial oxygen partial pressure rises from ~100 mmHg to ~1100 mmHg. Oxygen physically dissolved in plasma (Henry's law) diffuses into the transplanted follicles before their capillary network is restored.

card1.title: Session protocol
bullets: Session 1: Day Zero post-procedure, 60–90 min, 1.5–3.0 ATA
Session 2: day 1 post-procedure, 60–90 min
Optional booster sessions: day 4 and 7
Eligibility: no active ear infection, no untreated pneumothorax, no severe COPD

card2.title: Mechanism of action
card2.body: Oxygen oversaturation reduces the risk of graft necrosis during the ischemic window, suppresses HIF-1α activation linked to hypoxia, mobilizes endothelial progenitor cells from bone marrow (angiogenesis), and is bacteriostatic against anaerobic bacteria.
card2.mech: We partner with a certified hyperbaric therapy centre.

ladd.title: Microchannels instead of topical rubbing.
ladd.leadIntro: Laser-Assisted Drug Delivery is the controlled creation of vertical microchannels in the stratum corneum, enabling delivery of active substances (minoxidil, PRP, peptides, exosomes) down to the depth of the dermal papilla. Penetration efficacy increases several-fold compared with topical application.
ladd.leadWarning: Classical needle mesotherapy increases the risk of graft rejection because drug deposits can compress sprouting vessels and disrupt neovascularization. Many patients give up on follow-up treatments due to fear of pain. LADD laser protocols have been developed in collaboration with MySkinCode.pl

microbiome.title: Antisepsis that does not damage the graft.
microbiome.lead: Classical antiseptics (chlorhexidine, octenidine at higher concentrations, povidone-iodine) are cytotoxic to keratinocytes and fibroblasts in vitro. On a fresh post-procedural wound this is not neutral.

card1.title: HOCl — hypochlorous acid
card1.body: HOCl is the same compound that neutrophils produce during phagocytosis. At 0.01–0.02% it is bactericidal (including MRSA and S. aureus biofilms) and fungicidal against Malassezia, without cytotoxicity to grafts. Used as a contact-free spray for scalp cleansing from day 2.

card2.title: Botanical post-procedure formulas
card2.body: Sterile preservative-free gels based on extracts of Arnica montana (helenalin, dihydrohelenalin — erythema reduction) and Centella asiatica (madecassoside, asiaticoside — collagen I synthesis stimulation, anti-inflammatory). Applied over the donor area, which after DHI resembles an extensive abrasion.
card2.mech: Uncontrolled overgrowth of Malassezia and pathogenic Staphylococcus strains around micro-wounds promotes scar fibrosis and graft loss.

timeline.title: A chronological protocol, step by step.
timeline.lead: 48 hours = the critical window for graft survival. Full recovery is conducted systematically over the first 14 days.

phases.title: Ex Vivo phase — damage prevention
bullets: Grafts collected directly into HypoThermosol FRS + ATP-v, chilled to 4 °C
Graft bath in autologous PRP 10–20 min before implantation
Minimize ex vivo time: target < 4 h for the deepest grafts

phases.title: 48h — critical graft survival window (acute inflammation phase)
bullets: PBM 650 + 830 nm, 20 min, immediately after the procedure, then every 24 h
HBOT 1.5–3.0 ATA: session 1 (day 0), session 2 (day 1)
Donor area protected with preservative-free barrier ointment
Contact-free rinsing of the recipient area with HOCl from 48 h
Sleep in semi-sitting position (≥30°) for 5 days

phases.title: Proliferation phase — microbiome management
bullets: Scalp cleansing with HOCl or pH 5.5 shampoo without SLS, no rubbing
Home LLLT phototherapy (helmet) 2× daily/week, 20 min per session
From day 8: gentle massage to remove scabs + botanicals (arnica, centella)
Optical: erythema assessment, optional CAP session over the donor area

phases.title: Systemic support — anagen stimulation
bullets: Topical 5% minoxidil or oral microdoses 0.25–2.5 mg (off-label, after qualification)
PRP mesotherapy: sessions at month 1, 2, 4
LADD with thulium 1927 nm laser + minoxidil/PRP — from week 4–6
Maintenance PBM 1–2×/week for 12 weeks
Follow-up trichoscopy: month 3, 6, 12

card1.title: Graft survival
card1.p1: Hair transplant procedures (especially at reputable clinics) inherently achieve high survival of 90–95%[1].
card1.p2: RCTs show that using PBM (650 nm) does not spectacularly raise absolute survival (it is hard to exceed 95%), but it dramatically rescues grafts exposed to ischemia-reperfusion injury, statistically yielding 5–8%[2] more total accepted units compared to the placebo group.

card2.title: Faster anagen and healing
card2.p1: Normally, transplanted hairs enter telogen and shed after 2–4 weeks, with new anagen starting at month 3–4.
card2.p2: Studies show that patients irradiated with 655 nm enter anagen on average 3–4 weeks earlier[3]. Post-operative “shock loss” (telogen effluvium in the recipient area) is also reduced by about 20–30%[3,4].
card2.p3: Mixed-wavelength light (e.g. 633 nm + 830 nm) right after the procedure leads to scabs falling off 3–5 days faster. Objective (spectrophotometric) post-procedure erythema reduction is 30–40%[5] faster in the first 14 days.

card3.title: Final hair density and thickness
card3.alt: Animation of increased hair density and thickness
card3.p1: One year post-procedure, in groups using phototherapy (650 nm, 3×/week for 15–20 min), RCTs report an average increase of hair shaft diameter by 10–15%[3,4] and overall higher area density (not just from grafts, but also from stimulating miniaturized native hairs around the recipient zone).

card4.title: Revascularization and microcirculation
card4.p1: PBM (630–850 nm) increases VEGF expression and stimulates angiogenesis in the first days after the procedure, shortening the critical graft ischemia window and improving follicle nutrition.
card4.p2: HBOT (1.5–3.0 ATA) complements the mechanism — delivering plasma-dissolved oxygen to tissues with impaired perfusion until the new capillary network is fully restored.

risks.title: What can happen and when to stop the protocol immediately.
risks.lead: Every DHI hair transplant procedure involves natural, predictable bodily reactions. Below is a list of common side effects, contraindications and warning signs requiring immediate contact with the clinic.

card1.title: Side effects
items: Facial and forehead swelling, especially between day 2 and day 4 after the procedure.
Mild pinpoint bleeding from micro-wounds — typical for 24–48 h.
Pain, pressure and tightness of the scalp in the donor and recipient areas.
"Shock loss" — temporary loss of native hairs around new grafts.
Sensory disturbances (numbness, tingling) — usually resolve within 3–6 months.
Itching and flaking of the scalp during healing.
Infection — rare (<1%) when the antiseptic protocol is followed.

card2.title: Contraindications
items: Active bacterial, viral or fungal infections of the scalp.
Clotting disorders or use of (oral) anticoagulants.
Unstable diabetes — significantly impairs healing.
Active tobacco smoking — reduces graft survival by 20–30%.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (for certain pharmacological elements of the protocol).
Epilepsy or history of seizures — requires consultation before HBOT.
Bullous lung disease or abnormal pressure response — contraindication to hyperbaric therapy.

card3.title: Contact the clinic — alarms
items: Fever >38 °C after day 2 post-procedure.
Severe, increasing pain after day 3 (instead of subsiding).
Redness, swelling and purulent discharge from the recipient or donor area.
Open wounds, partial loss or "extrusion" of grafts.
Allergic symptoms: hives, shortness of breath, facial swelling.
Fainting, severe dizziness or ear pain after an HBOT session.
Bleeding that does not stop after 10 min of gauze pressure.
card3.mech: Do not wait until morning to make contact. In the critical 48 h window, every hour of delay can affect graft survival.
